chapter: Oliver, Kelly and the district bands
title: Lavasheaux's string band and unsteady personnel
summary: The violinist's band had no standard men; musicians jumped bands for better tips.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did you have a violin in your band that everyone wanted to?
Um, yeah, we did. That's right. We had, we had Jimmy Palau. Oh, yeah. Jimmy Palau played Bobby. I believe he's dead.
Yeah, I never really get the door ever hearing.
Too bad. You were speaking about this O'Neal Lavasheaux, is that his name? Lavasheaux, yeah. Lavasheaux. Yeah, O'Neal Lavasheaux. Can you remember, how many was in his, it was a string band, though?
Yeah, he's a regular dance band, you know. Is it a fire piece, do you think? Fire piece, yeah. Violin, uh, violin, guitar, bass, and, no, didn't have no bass. They had drum and piano.
Oh. You don't know any of the men that were playing, besides the...

Well, I'll tell you, he never had no standard men, you know. He just, uh, sometime, you know, he'd change in different men, you know, half of the time. Uh-oh. Because, uh, at that time, there was so much work going on, you had a hard time keeping a man on one job, you know. Saying, like, this week he'd have a man, and next week he'd have a different man all the time. That's the way he was, you see. Couldn't keep a man on, cause the job wasn't that big, you know. And the tips wasn't that good there, you see. And the fellas, musicians, was jumping from band to band. Anytime they'd get a good opening where they had more money to be made, that was jumping. That's the way it was going. They were running from one... Couldn't keep a good man in one spot. Well, he'd had his place over there, the tips wasn't so much at few close places, you see. And, uh, dead bull, they ain't work, make a night or two nights, and after that, then... Gone, you know, you'd have to get another man, you see.
